sources.README.md:
# Laboratory microscopy series upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Node 22.23.2.
Dependencies: Vue 3.4.38; jsdom 22.1.0; esbuild 0.21.5. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

The mounted component delegates synchronous select/retry/hide commands to its
session, projects state through the actual framework, and disposes its session
on lifecycle teardown. The source uses EventTarget and AbortController; decode
may return a value or Promise. jQuery commands use synchronous triggerHandler.

rules.body:
Apply when a shared progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, full-frame decoding may finish later, and history and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order." Confirm these premises and the target's display-order requirement before applying freshness suppression.

Register panel reception before invoking startup, preserving later streaming. Original src/workflow.go: "env.Call("start",file.Token);subscription=env.Call("listen",file.Token,callback)". TASK: "Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior." Make retirement effective during startup so subsequent packets cannot start new work through an obsolete subscription, even before the outer startup returns. Keep already admitted decoding separate from that admission decision.

When the task requires full-frame freshness, assign ordering at packet reception before decoding or callback-capable work. Scope ordering to the display owner, including attempts sharing one visit. After a newer frame has been published, suppress older frames only from presentation. Recheck both visit authority and publication order after audit callbacks; commit the publication watermark before calling the display sink, which may reenter delivery. TASK: "Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward." README.md: "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Reception order, rather than loaded magnitude or completion order, determines freshness. Buffering every result until arrival order can be reconstructed is not required.

Keep audit completion independent of display permission. Capture the originating file, attempt and visit; retain the existing audit effect for each admitted decode, including completion after hide, replacement, cancellation or disposal. Audit before deciding whether to paint, then recheck visit authority and freshness because audit may synchronously navigate or complete another decode. README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." Original src/workflow.go: "deliver:=func(frame interface{}){;audit(frame);view(frame,order)}". A stale display frame still retains its history effect.

Coordinate ownership across callback-capable startup and cleanup. Publish cleanup ownership before startup callbacks can navigate; reconcile the returned handle without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation. Remove old resources from current ownership before canceling them, and recheck the navigation request after cleanup returns. Cancel captured retired resources and preserve repeated cleanup behavior. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle." README.md: "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred." Preserve cancellation order from src/workflow.go: "h.CancelContext();h.Stop();h.Env.Call("cancel",h.File.Token,h.Number)". A provisional handle is an implementation option, not a required public API.

Keep an accepted retry bound to its entry visit and file across cancellation reentry. Cancel the previous attempt before enqueueing, retain the accepted command's record and attempt creation, cancel its resulting attempt if its visit has ended, and publish its queued notice only while that visit remains current. Original src/workflow.go: "v.Handle.Cancel();accepted:=v;h:=s.enqueue(accepted,"retry");if s.current(accepted){accepted.Handle=h}else{h.Cancel()};if s.current(accepted){s.notice(accepted,h)}". Preserve record-before-transport ordering, independent session counters and disposal. Preserve the exact queue fields from src/workflow.go: "entry:=map[string]interface{}{"fileId":v.File.ID,"attemptId":n,"visitId":v.ID,"kind":kind}" and notice fields: "map[string]interface{}{"fileId":v.File.ID,"attemptId":h.Number,"visitId":v.ID,"status":"queued"}".

Do not generalize panel reception or freshness changes to diagnostic consumers, introduce numeric monotonicity, extend queue records, or discard required audit. README.md: "The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/\ncollectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate\nfrom the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance." README.md: "Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}\nunless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size." Conversely, do not transfer an earlier task's absence of out-of-order display requirements into a target whose TASK explicitly requires freshness protection.

Candidate limitations:
- Only TASK and the supplied public documents and source establish requirements. Automatic contracts, prior experiences and evaluation observations do not.
- Attempt 1 reports passing syntax and acceptance checks, but supplies no behavioral observations establishing completeness, causality or cross-task benefit.
- Rejected decoding, adapter exceptions and physical transfer completion are outside the documented model.
- Cancellation does not establish a requirement to discard decoding already accepted by an older attempt while its visit remains current.
- The earlier experience's lack of a freshness requirement applied to its earlier sources. This task explicitly requires freshness protection; that difference does not invalidate the earlier task's boundary.
- No workspace files were modified and no scorer, reference implementation or hidden tests were accessed.

Check cached startup and later streaming; immediate and deferred decoding; newer-then-older completion with both audit effects retained; and later packets whose loaded values decrease. Exercise nested delivery from audit and display callbacks to verify authority checks and watermark commitment. Navigate during startup, emit another packet before startup returns, and verify retired admission, cleanup, newer ownership and subsequent delivery. Complete admitted decoding after hide, replacement and disposal; reopen the identical file as a new visit. Exercise navigation from unlisten and cancellation, accepted entry-bound retries, retired queued-notice suppression, repeated cleanup, independent sessions, unchanged payloads and unchanged telemetry. These checks follow TASK's preservation and freshness requirements and README.md's synchronous callback model. checkpoints: Warm panel source: install panel reception, call start, synchronously emit cached progress, and verify the initial frame is decoded, audited, and displayed.
Ordinary streaming: emit later packets through the same target and verify they continue to decode, audit, and display.
Out-of-order decoding: receive older then newer packets, resolve newer first and older last, and verify both are audited while the older completion does not replace the newer displayed frame.
Legitimate reset: receive a later packet whose loaded value is lower and verify it can replace the earlier display; freshness is based on reception order, not numeric progress.
Retry: verify retry remains in the same visit, freshness spans its attempts, the prior attempt is canceled, and queue records/notices retain their existing identities and shapes.

Startup reentrancy: during synchronous start delivery, select, hide, reopen the same file, or dispose; verify the retired visit admits no later packet, newer ownership survives, and already-admitted decoding retains its audit effect.
Audit reentrancy: navigate or complete newer progress from recordProgress, then verify authority and freshness are rechecked before display.
Display reentrancy: trigger nested delivery/navigation from showProgress and verify the publication watermark and current visit cannot be rolled back.
Cleanup: remove a listener through cancellation, including reentrant host navigation, and verify removal is committed, repeated removal is inert, and newer resources remain owned.

Diagnostic telemetry: verify collectProgressTelemetry retains its existing start-before-listen behavior and observes subsequent live decoded deltas without receiving the panel-specific cached bootstrap.
Subsequent use: after hide, replacement, cancellation, or disposal where applicable, reopen/select again—including the identical file object—and verify the new visit operates independently.
Run the public JavaScript/Vue syntax or build checks after an Action; treat them only as syntax/build checks, not proof of business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not change public transfer invocation, cancellation notification, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, notice, or queue-record behavior beyond lifecycle coordination required to restore panel bootstrap safely.
Do not add fields such as byteCount to queue records; their authorized shape remains {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
Do not suppress recordProgress for an admitted frame merely because its visit or attempt was later canceled, hidden, replaced, or disposed.
Do not use loaded magnitude as freshness: a later full frame may legitimately decrease or reset displayed progress.
Do not apply panel bootstrap reception or full-frame freshness filtering to collectProgressTelemetry.
Do not let an obsolete startup, cleanup callback, or decode completion overwrite a newer visit or its resource ownership.
Do not treat selecting the same file object again as continuation of the former visit.
Do not infer requirements from automatic findings, experience, evaluation observations, hidden tests, or reference implementations.
lifecycle_identity: A panel visit is created by each select operation; selecting the identical file object again creates a distinct visit.
A retry creates a new physical attempt but remains within its accepted entry visit.
Attempt identity is distinct from visit identity and uses the session's attempt counter.
Progress history identity is the originating file, attempt, and frame; visible eligibility additionally depends on the originating visit still being current.
Display freshness belongs to the visit and therefore spans retries within that visit; a new visit starts a new display-order lifetime.
Each Session/workspace has its own lifetime, visit ownership, counters, and publication state.
The diagnostic telemetry listener has a separate consumer lifetime and is not panel visit state.

obligations.text: For panel progress, register the progress listener before invoking feed.start() so a synchronously emitted cached packet can produce the initial progress update and later packets continue through the same listener.

Before decoding a received panel packet, require that its originating subscription has not been retired and its originating visit is still authoritative; retirement during synchronous startup must prevent admission of subsequent packets even if physical cleanup has not yet been returned or completed.

Assign panel frame order at packet reception, before decoding. When decoded completions arrive out of order, an earlier-received frame must not replace a later-received frame that has already been displayed.
Scope the display publication order to the visit, including all retry attempts in that visit. Do not compare loaded values because later full frames may decrease or reset.

Every admitted decode completion retains its existing audit call exactly once, even if cancellation, hide, replacement, or disposal occurs before completion; stale-display suppression must not suppress this audit.
After audit returns, recheck both current-visit authority and publication freshness before calling showProgress, because host callbacks are synchronous and may navigate or publish other progress.
Commit the visit's publication watermark before calling showProgress so synchronous reentry cannot allow an older completion to roll the display backward.

Coordinate startup and cleanup ownership so navigation during synchronous start, listener removal, cancellation, audit, or display cannot let an older operation replace or cancel resources owned by newer navigation; retired resources must still be cleaned up.

Preserve retry behavior: cancel the prior attempt before enqueueing the accepted retry, keep that retry bound to its entry visit and file, retain its queue record, cancel its resulting handle if the visit ended during callbacks, and publish its queued notice only while that visit is current.
Preserve the diagnostic collectProgressTelemetry sequence and behavior independently from the panel repair: it continues to call start before registering its listener and records decoded live deltas.

Preserve subsequent reuse: removal is committed before the host detach callback, repeated removal is inert, and a later visit—including one for the same file object—can receive and display its own progress.
Preserve component delegation and teardown: synchronous select/retry/hide commands continue to delegate to Session, and lifecycle teardown continues to dispose the Session.

recordProgress retains the originating fileId and attemptId and remains independent from visible panel eligibility.

# Laboratory microscopy series upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Node 22.23.2.
Dependencies: Vue 3.4.38; jsdom 22.1.0; esbuild 0.21.5. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

The mounted component delegates synchronous select/retry/hide commands to its
session, projects state through the actual framework, and disposes its session
on lifecycle teardown. The source uses EventTarget and AbortController; decode
may return a value or Promise. jQuery commands use synchronous triggerHandler.
